stem.en: How does the Ṛig Veda describe ṛita?

text.en: As a list of duties for students at a gurukula.
As the name of the first king of the Vedic people.
As an all-pervading cosmic order that stands for harmony and balance in nature and human society.
As a tax paid by villages to the ruler.

explanation.en: The Ṛig Veda describes ṛita as an all-pervading cosmic order representing harmony and balance in nature and in human society. It regulates the forces of nature and upholds moral values.

hints.en: It covers both nature and society.
